name: coinbase_lead_lag_premise
status: pre-registered (amended twice, both before any data was read); not run; no spot_ticks data has been read
question: Does the 60-second CF Benchmarks RTI lag pure, venue-labelled Coinbase prints by 1-3 seconds, often enough and by enough to support a settlement-average trade, and does a Coinbase-based settlement probability beat the market's own mid?

data.coinbase: spot_ticks rows with source == 'coinbase' only (kraken and rest are excluded), exported read-only from data/openkal-prod.db into spot_ticks.npz
data.rti: index_*.npz (ts, value, accum, k) from the pinned tape
data.books_and_outcomes: book_*.npz and markets.json from the same pinned tape

run_gate.meaning: about three full days of 15-minute windows; below this the script writes status insufficient_data and computes no statistic

eligibility.window: a distinct 15-minute close is eligible when all four lanes have a settled outcome and, for every lane, the Coinbase prints in [close - 150 s, close] number at least 30 with a largest gap of at most 3.0 s

split.rule: chronological over the eligible closes: cut = eligible_closes[int(0.6 * n)]; IS = closes below the cut
split.oos: closes at or above the cut are never read by this test and stay sealed for any later sweep
split.reads: only rows with ts < cut are used by the lead-lag statistic; the funnel and Brier use windows closing before the cut

lead_lag.series: per second, the last Coinbase print and the last RTI print at or before t, each used only when at most fresh_s old
lead_lag.statistic: r_cb(t) = ln cb(t) - ln cb(t-1) and r_rti(t) = ln rti(t) - ln rti(t-1) on the integer-second grid (a return needs both prices fresh). For lag k: A_k = corr(r_cb(t), r_rti(t+k)) - corr(r_rti(t), r_cb(t+k)), Pearson over all t with both returns finite. Positive A_k means Coinbase's move k seconds earlier predicts the RTI's move better than the reverse. Primary statistic S = A_1 + A_2; A_5 is reported only.

bootstrap.method: resample 15-minute blocks (floor(t / 900)) of per-second rows with replacement; percentile interval of S

lead_lag.lane_passes_when: S >= 0.10 and the bootstrap lower bound of S is above 0
lead_lag.criterion_passes_when: at least 3 of the 4 lanes pass
lead_lag.horizon_5: A_5 is reported only; it should be near zero if the lag is 1-3 s
lead_lag.effect_size_note: 0.10 is about a sixth of the lag-0 return correlation seen on the engine spot (0.61); on that unlabelled spot A_1 = 0.160 - 0.227 and A_2 = 0.026 - 0.080, so S was about -0.12

funnel.rti_state: AsianRTI.fair() returns a state (venue-locked accumulator accepted)
funnel.event: a (lane, window) with at least one row meeting all of the above
funnel.criterion_passes_when: at least 100 events across at least 40 distinct window closes

brier.model: p_cb_asian: P(mean of the 60 fixings >= strike) with the Coinbase print standing in for every fixing still to come (scripts/track8_coinbase_rti_settle.asian_p)
brier.difference: d = (p_cb - y)^2 - (mid - y)^2 per row, y the YES outcome; also reported: the RTI-spot probability and the mid, each on the same rows
brier.criterion_passes_when: mean d < 0 and the 95% bootstrap upper bound of mean d is below 0

decision.premise_passes_when: lead_lag AND funnel AND brier all pass
decision.on_pass: a sweep may be designed on IS only; the OOS slice stays sealed until the sweep has an IS champion
decision.on_fail: no sweep; the premise is closed
decision.single_run: the script refuses to run again once a decided receipt exists

prior_to_beat.source: independent backtest on 23.5k windows, supplied by the owner
claims: no taker edge at a 5 s or longer delay
in the final 60 s the market predicted settlement better than public feeds (Brier 0.004 against 0.039)

known_before_registering: Track 8 used the engine's unlabelled tick spot (Coinbase, Kraken or REST). On BTC its 1 s return correlation with the index was 0.609 at lag 0, 0.227 with the index return a second before and 0.160 a second after, i.e. no lead over the index.
Track 8's 8 bps divergence funnel on that spot was 5 rows in 3 lane-windows in sample; the live-spot repricing lost money even without the divergence trigger.
disclosure: The thresholds above were set after seeing those Track 8 results. The expectation is that the premise fails; the bar is meant to be hard.

amendments.reason: v1 measured lead-lag with a past window x over (t-h, t] against a future window y over (t, t+h] and required both h=1 and h=2 to pass. A pure RTI lag of 2 s or 3 s leaves no overlap at h=1 (the lagged move lies before the past window), so v1 could fail a true 1-3 s lag, which is the premise being tested. It also said 'five prices' where the statistic used six. Replaced by exact-lag correlations of 1-second returns.
amendments.made_before: any code for the premise test, any run, and any read of spot_ticks data

amendments.reason: The clock basis of the two series was not stated. Read from source: spot_ticks.ts is the engine host's time.time() when the Coinbase print callback ran; the index ts is the Kalshi websocket frame's received_at field (milliseconds, a Kalshi-side clock) when present, else the host's time.time(). A lead-lag statistic at 1-2 s therefore compares 'Coinbase as our host saw it' with 'RTI as Kalshi stamped it'.
amendments.made_before: any run and any read of spot_ticks data
amendments.not_changed: no threshold, rule, window, split, bootstrap setting or criterion

clock_basis.coinbase_ts: spot_ticks.ts = the engine host's time.time() when the print callback ran (openkal/engine.py _on_price)
clock_basis.rti_ts: index_*.npz ts = the Kalshi websocket frame's received_at (ms, Kalshi-side clock) when present, else the host's time.time() (openkal/kalshi_ws.py _handle_index)
clock_basis.meaning: A pass reads: Coinbase prints as stamped by our host lead the RTI as stamped by Kalshi by 1-2 seconds.
clock_basis.not_measured: the host-versus-Kalshi clock offset and each feed's network latency; the 1 s grid assigns most prints to the same second for any offset under about half a second, and a real lead of a second or more is far above NTP-scale offsets, but this is not verified
clock_basis.tradeability: the lead as seen by our host in real time is what a trade could use; the Brier criterion, not the lead-lag statistic, is what tests whether anything of value follows from it
